can_do_statement: Can use the past perfect simple after 'because' to give explanatory information.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Providing background explanations with 'because' + past perfect

positives: I was driving on to my parents' house because I had arranged to have dinner with them.
He was sleeping but I realised that this was because he had lost a lot of blood.
negatives: I am doing this because I have lost my keys.
We stayed inside because it had a bad smell.

guideword: FORM/USE: AFTER 'IF ONLY' AND 'WISH', IMAGINED PAST
can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative form after 'if only', and the affirmative and negative forms after 'wish' to talk about regret.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Regret over past events with 'wish' or 'if only' + past perfect

positives: If only I had listened to my father when he warned me!
I wish I hadn't told Pat about my plans.
negatives: I wish I had a car right now.
If only she would listen to me.

can_do_statement: Can use the past perfect simple to talk about a time before another time in the past.

ontology.mental_model: Sequencing a past action before another past point
ontology.pedagogical_hook: The "past in the past" for narrative timeline building

positives: He then thought how stupid he had been.
Actually I'd arranged an appointment with my doctor before calling you.
negatives: I have arranged a meeting for tomorrow.
She had a really great time at the party.

can_do_statement: Can use the past perfect simple with a wide range of adverbs (including 'finally', 'recently', 'simply') in the normal mid-position.  ► adverbs

ontology.mental_model: Modifying prior completed actions with adverbials
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Mid-position adverbs between auxiliary 'had' and past participle

positives: He had finally achieved his goal after years of work!
She had suddenly woken up at that noise.
negatives: I had walked there quickly.
He had been a teacher recently.

can_do_statement: Can invert the subject and auxiliary verb with 'no sooner … than' to talk about something that happened immediately before something else, often in formal contexts.

ontology.mental_model: Emphasising immediate sequence of past events via inversion
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Formal inversion: 'No sooner had I...' to add dramatic sequencing

positives: No sooner had I gone to bed than someone broke the door down.
But, no sooner had I got there than my classmates informed me.
negatives: I had no sooner finished my work than the bell rang.
We will leave no sooner than 8 PM.

ontology.mental_model: Inquiring about events completed before a past reference point

positives: Had I made the same mistake twice?
The question was: Why had he done that?
negatives: I asked why he had done that.
Had a great time yesterday?

can_do_statement: Can invert the subject and auxiliary verb after 'never (before)' to talk about a unique event, often in formal contexts.

ontology.mental_model: Emphasising uniqueness of a past experience through inversion
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Formal emphatic phrasing with 'Never had I...'

positives: Never had I been in such a ridiculous situation!
Never before had we seen such marvellous species of fish.
negatives: I had never been in such a situation.
She will never have time for that.

can_do_statement: Can leave out the subject before the past perfect simple where it is understood from the previous clause.

ontology.mental_model: Linking sequential facts while omitting redundant subjects
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Compound predicates sharing a single subject into the past perfect

positives: Simon was a very famous writer and had written ten best-sellers.
They were cold and had gone numb.
negatives: Simon was a writer and he had written ten best-sellers.
She smiled, and had a piece of cake.

can_do_statement: Can invert the subject and affirmative auxiliary verb to talk about imagined situations in the past, often with regret, in formal contexts.

positives: Had I known the tour would be so bad, I wouldn't have booked it.
Sometimes I think that had I gone to Britain without this experience, my life would be different.
negatives: Had I known the answer?
If I had known the tour would be so bad, I wouldn't have booked it.

can_do_statement: Can use the past perfect simple to report statements, where the main verb in the reporting clause is in the past simple.  ► reported speech

ontology.mental_model: Backshifting past facts into reported speech
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Past simple reporting verb + past perfect reported clause

positives: She tried to explain what had happened, but she couldn't.
I looked at the address and I knew what had happened to my sister's postcard.
negatives: She says what had happened.
He explained what is happening now.

can_do_statement: Can use the past perfect simple to talk about situations which changed.

ontology.mental_model: Contrasting an earlier plan or state with a subsequent change
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Past perfect of intention (planned/wanted) contrasting with 'but'

positives: We had planned to go to Switzerland, but unfortunately our car broke down.
At first she had wanted to make the first move but she wasn't quite convinced.
negatives: I had hoped she would come.
We planned to go to the park, but it rained.

can_do_statement: Can use the past perfect simple in relative clauses to give background information.    ► relative clauses

ontology.mental_model: Adding preceding context via relative modifiers
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Relative pronoun + past perfect for background details

positives: It was Annika who had arranged a huge party for her.
He went to the hotel to find out who the person was that had sent him a mysterious letter.
negatives: She found the book which she bought yesterday.
Who had arranged this?

can_do_statement: Can use the past perfect simple to report questions, where the main verb in the reporting clause is in the past simple.  ► reported speech

ontology.mental_model: Backshifting past questions into reported speech
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Past reporting verb + wh-word/if + past perfect

positives: I asked him who had given him my phone number.
He asked me if I had seen her somewhere.
negatives: I asked him who gave him my phone number.
She wondered what he is doing.

guideword: FORM: FIXED EXPRESSIONS 'HAD IT NOT BEEN FOR', 'IF IT HADN'T BEEN FOR'
can_do_statement: Can use 'had it not been for' … and 'if it hadn’t been for' with a modal form for giving reasons.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Fixed idioms for attributing negative causality: 'had it not been for'

positives: Had it not been for the fact that I had already read the article, I would have thought otherwise.
If it hadn't been for my lack of knowledge, I wouldn't have been fired.
negatives: It had not been for sale at that time.
If it hasn't been for long, we can wait.

can_do_statement: Can use the negative form after 'if only' to express regret.

positives: If only she had not changed, we would still be best friends.
If only I hadn't been that rude!
negatives: If only I had listened to you.
If only they wouldn't do that.
